descriptions.publisher: Publisher name (e.g., Elsevier, Springer Nature, Wiley), known from the collection configuration for each source.
descriptions.journal: Journal title as listed on the publisher website.
descriptions.editor: Editor full name as it appeared on the editorial board page, after mojibake repair and light cleaning.
descriptions.role: Role label as listed on the publisher page, unmodified.
descriptions.role_std: Standardized role, one of exactly ten canonical values: editor_in_chief, senior_editor, deputy_editor, associate_editor, section_editor, reviewing_editor, guest_editor, editorial_board_member, editor, other. The mapping is deterministic from the raw role string and, for the two fallbacks named below, the rest of the journal's board. editor_in_chief is the journal's chief, singular or plural, in English, French, German, Spanish or Portuguese. A rank written before the chief keeps that rank: associate, deputy, vice and assistant chiefs are deputy_editor, and section chiefs and Frontiers specialty chiefs are section_editor, except that a journal with no other chief keeps its specialty chiefs as editor_in_chief. An assistant to the Editor-in-Chief is not a chief, while former, past, founding, honorary and emeritus chiefs keep editor_in_chief. Advisory and consulting roles and collective names of the board (editorial or scientific committees, councils and panels, also in French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian and German) are editorial_board_member; academic, handling and action editors are associate_editor; book review editors are section_editor. 'senior_editor' was introduced in v3.0.0. 'other' holds staff roles (managing editors, associate and deputy ones included, the editorial office and its assistants, publishing, production, technical and social-media editors, publishers), unless the heading also names an editor of the journal or the journal's board has no other editor-type role, in which case its managing and technical editors are editor; 'other' also holds roles that match no canonical value, together roughly 2% of positions.
descriptions.role_is_former: True when the raw role names a position its holder has left or holds in name: the words past, previous, former, founding, founder, honorary, retired, deceased and in memoriam, any word beginning with emerit (emeritus, emerita, emeriti, emérito, émérite), ex- before an editorial title, and their French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Italian forms (ancien, honoraire, fondateur, ehemalig, Ehren-, Gründungs-, fundador, honorario, onorario, fondatore), in any case and in any role, as in 'Former Editors-in-Chief', 'Editor Emeritus', 'Past Editorial Board Members' or 'Honorary Editorial Board'. role_std ignores these words, so a former chief is still an editor_in_chief: exclude these rows to study the boards as they serve. Not flagged: a role that says ex officio, whose holder serves by virtue of an office now; a society officer's title such as Past President or Immediate Past Chair; a personal academic title such as Emeritus Professor, Professor Emeritus, Honorary Fellow or Founding Director; past and present (or former and current) together; and outgoing editors, still serving when the page was read. Computed from the raw role alone: a row whose raw role is empty is False. Founding and honorary do not always mean that the person no longer serves: a founding editor may still lead the journal, and an honorary board may be a current one. A heading that names a former and a current role at once, such as 'Founding Editor and Editor-in-Chief', flags every row under it. The flag says what the heading says. True on 10,533 records (1.1%), 1,913 of them editor_in_chief.
descriptions.affiliation: Institutional affiliation as listed, after universal cleaning (strips roles, credentials, dates, junk). Not canonicalised; see ror_name for the authoritative form.
descriptions.orcid: 16-digit ORCID iD. Preferred from the collected value when available; otherwise backfilled from OpenAlex or the ORCID API (see orcid_source).
descriptions.source_url: Public publisher URL of the journal's editorial board: the page this record was collected from or, where the publisher has since moved its board, the corrected address (from Mir@bel's corrections and the rules behind them).
descriptions.scraped_at: ISO-8601 timestamp of when this record was collected. The column name is retained for backward compatibility with earlier releases.
descriptions.gender_raw: Backwards-compatibility column kept since v1; mirrors gender exactly (WGND has no mostly_male / mostly_female granularity). Retained so v1-era scripts keep running; new work should read gender.
descriptions.ror_id: Research Organization Registry identifier resolved from the raw affiliation string via the ROR /organizations?affiliation= fuzzy-match endpoint, subject to score and token-overlap guards (see CHANGELOG v2.0.0) that reject low-confidence matches. Some organisations draw clusters of false matches (issue #30), and a match to one of them is kept only when the affiliation names that organisation. v4.0.0 re-applied the v2.0.0 repair, which later re-enrichments had undone, to the organisations then known. North Central State College and College Station Medical Center were added after v5.0.0: through their ROR aliases ("NC State", "The Med") they took North Carolina State University and abbreviated hospital addresses.
descriptions.ror_name: Canonical institution name from the ROR v2 record (ror_display name).
descriptions.ror_country: Country name from ROR/GeoNames for the primary location of the institution.
descriptions.ror_state: State or province of the primary location in the ROR record of the row's ror_id, as ROR gives it: usually a name, occasionally a GeoNames code (e.g. SG.01); empty when the ROR record gives none. Taken from ROR for every row with a ror_id since v4.0.1.
descriptions.ror_city: City of the primary location in the ROR record of the row's ror_id (GeoNames). Taken from ROR for every row with a ror_id since v4.0.1, which filled 5,537 rows left empty in v4.0.0.
descriptions.org_type: Organization type from ROR: education, healthcare, government, facility, nonprofit, company, archive, or other. Taken from the first entry in the ROR record's types array.
descriptions.latitude: Geographic latitude of the institution from ROR/GeoNames.
descriptions.longitude: Geographic longitude of the institution from ROR/GeoNames.
descriptions.scientific_domain: OpenAlex domain of scientific_field (Health Sciences, Life Sciences, Physical Sciences or Social Sciences), or Multidisciplinary. Journal-level: identical for every editor of a journal.
descriptions.scientific_field: Journal-level OpenAlex field (e.g. Medicine, Engineering, Psychology), identical for every editor of a journal: it describes the journal, not the editor's own research. Since v4.0.0 it is the field of most of the journal's own research articles with an abstract, by primary topic (falling back to all articles, then all works, below 30 classified works), provided that field covers at least 40% of those articles or the journal's earlier topic was one of OpenAlex's catch-all topics. Otherwise the journal keeps its v3.0.0 classification, which came from its most frequent OpenAlex topic. Multidisciplinary for journals the Norwegian Register for Scientific Journals (NPI) files under Interdisciplinary Natural Sciences. Empty when OpenAlex has no classified works for the journal.
descriptions.scientific_subfield: Journal-level OpenAlex subfield. For journals classified by their articles (see scientific_field), the most common subfield among those articles within scientific_field; for journals that keep the v3.0.0 classification, the subfield of their most frequent OpenAlex topic. Empty for Multidisciplinary journals.
descriptions.scientific_topic: Journal-level OpenAlex topic. For journals classified by their articles (see scientific_field), the most common topic among those articles within scientific_subfield; for journals that keep the v3.0.0 classification, their most frequent OpenAlex topic. Empty for Multidisciplinary journals.
descriptions.openalex_source_id: OpenAlex Source identifier for the journal, resolved from the journal title and/or ISSN. In v5.0.0, the journals that the ISSN-L audit found matched to another journal's source take their own journal's source, or none where no source can be trusted, and their journal metrics, indexing, NPI and classification follow it. In v4.0.0, 152 journals whose recorded source OpenAlex had since retired were moved to the current source for their ISSN-L, and their four oa_ journal metrics were refreshed from it in September 2026; the other journals keep the metrics from the original enrichment.
descriptions.issn_l: Linking ISSN (the ISSN-L groups print and electronic variants into one identifier) from OpenAlex. Since v5.0.0 it has been checked against the journal's title and publisher; empty where no OpenAlex source can be trusted.
descriptions.issn_print: ISSN of the journal's print version, written NNNN-NNNC with its check digit verified, as typed by the NLM Catalog's list of journals (Source: National Library of Medicine), else DOAJ's journal metadata, else Crossref's journal record (issn-type). The two catalogues come first: Crossref's types are the publishers' deposits, and some publishers deposit an online-only journal's one ISSN as print, so a lone print ISSN from Crossref is not used for a publisher whose lone print ISSNs the catalogues often contradict. Taken only from a record that lists the journal's ISSN-L, and given only when the ISSN-L is the print or the electronic ISSN (an ISSN-L is one of the ISSNs of the journal's media, ISO 3297); a Crossref record must also carry the journal's title, unless it is a renamed journal's own record (the journal's OpenAlex source carries the journal's title and lists every ISSN the record types, one of them other than the ISSN-L), so another title's record cannot supply it. Empty where no source types one, where a source is ambiguous (two print ISSNs, or one number typed both ways), where the journal has no ISSN-L, or where its ISSN-L fails its own check digit. The same on every row of a journal. The ISSN International Centre's register is not used: its licence does not allow redistribution in a public-domain dataset.
descriptions.issn_electronic: ISSN of the journal's electronic version (E-ISSN), written NNNN-NNNC with its check digit verified, as typed by the NLM Catalog's list of journals (Source: National Library of Medicine), else DOAJ's journal metadata, else Crossref's journal record (issn-type). Taken only from a record that lists the journal's ISSN-L, and given only when the ISSN-L is the print or the electronic ISSN (an ISSN-L is one of the ISSNs of the journal's media, ISO 3297); a Crossref record must also carry the journal's title, unless it is a renamed journal's own record (the journal's OpenAlex source carries the journal's title and lists every ISSN the record types, one of them other than the ISSN-L), so another title's record cannot supply it. Never equal to issn_print. Empty where no source types one, where a source is ambiguous, where the journal has no ISSN-L, or where its ISSN-L fails its own check digit. The same on every row of a journal.
descriptions.issn_type_source: Which open sources typed issn_print and issn_electronic: nlm (the NLM Catalog's list of journals), doaj (DOAJ's journal metadata) or crossref (Crossref's journal record), or two of them joined by + in that order when each gave one column (nlm+crossref: NLM gave one, Crossref the other), in which case both columns are filled. A source that types a column differently from an earlier one is overruled; the OpenAlex source's ISSN list, which is not typed, only cross-checks the result. Empty when both ISSN columns are empty.
descriptions.oa_2yr_mean_citedness: OpenAlex 2-year mean citedness: average citations received by articles published in the last 2 years. Open-data analogue of the Clarivate Journal Impact Factor but computed from OpenAlex citation graph.
descriptions.oa_journal_works_count: Total number of works published in the journal (OpenAlex count).
descriptions.oa_journal_cited_by_count: Total citations received by the journal (OpenAlex count).
descriptions.is_in_doaj: True if the journal is listed in the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ).
descriptions.is_oa: True if OpenAlex classifies the journal as open access.
descriptions.h_index: Author h-index from OpenAlex, looked up by (name, ror_id) pair.
descriptions.total_publications: Total number of works by this author in OpenAlex.
descriptions.total_citations: Total citations received by this author in OpenAlex.
descriptions.academic_age: Years since this author's first OpenAlex-indexed publication (current year minus earliest publication year).
descriptions.orcid_source: Provenance of the ORCID iD. Values: 'scraped' (the iD was published on the editorial board page itself), 'missing' (no iD resolved for this record), and 'cleared_cross_institution_backfill' (a previously backfilled iD that was withdrawn in v2.x because the candidate profile resolved to a different institution than the editor's, and so could not be trusted).
descriptions.name_script: Detected writing script of the editor's name (Latin, CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic, etc.). Used to document coverage gaps in downstream inference steps.
descriptions.name_script_region: Geographic region associated with the name script. Heuristic, not authoritative.
descriptions.indexed_pubmed: True if the journal is indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE (matched on ISSN against the NLM catalog).
descriptions.indexed_scopus: True if the journal is indexed in Scopus (matched on ISSN against the Scopus source list).
descriptions.indexed_wos: True if the journal is indexed in Web of Science (matched on ISSN against the WoS master journal list).
descriptions.indexed_doaj: True if the journal is listed in the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ).
descriptions.indexed_cope: True if the publisher is a member of COPE (Committee on Publication Ethics). Publisher-level flag applied to all of that publisher's journals.
descriptions.indexed_npi: True if the journal appears in the Norwegian Publishing Indicator register (at either level 1 or level 2). See the separate 'Norwegian Publishing Indicator' group below for the level and discipline fields.
descriptions.npi_level: Norwegian Publishing Indicator level. Level 2 marks the top ~20% of journals in the register; level 1 is the remainder of the register; 0 and X denote entries the register carries without a scoring level. Scope is limited to Nordic-relevant disciplines. Stored as a string. Earlier releases carried the float spellings '1.0' and '2.0' on some rows; v5.0.0 folded them into '1' and '2', and 0 rows carry them now.
descriptions.npi_discipline: Broad discipline in the NPI register.
descriptions.npi_field: Specific field in the NPI register.
descriptions.indexing_count: Sum of the indexed_* flags (PubMed, Scopus, WoS, DOAJ, COPE, NPI). Range 0–6. A rough journal-quality proxy independent of citation metrics. Used as the indexing weight in the experimental 'weighted power' score on the Network page.
descriptions.oa_impact_quartile: Q1 to Q4, computed locally by this project within each scientific_field from oa_2yr_mean_citedness. A journal's position is the share of journals in the same field with strictly lower citedness: Q4 below 0.25, Q3 below 0.50, Q2 below 0.75, Q1 from 0.75. Q1 is therefore roughly the top quarter of the field, so the value accounts for differing citation norms across disciplines, and journals with equal citedness share a quartile. Empty when the journal has no field or no citedness, or its field has fewer than 4 such journals. Releases up to v3.0.0 published one split across all journals despite this description; see CHANGELOG. This is NOT the Clarivate JIF or the Scopus CiteScore quartile.
descriptions.top_funder_1: Most common funding organization for articles in this journal (from the OpenAlex Works funder metadata).
descriptions.top_funder_1_count: Number of funded articles from the top funder.
descriptions.data_version: Dataset version stamp for the row, matching CHANGELOG.md. 2026.6 for the v6.0.0 release (v4.0.0: 2026.3). Stored as a number, not a string.
descriptions.enriched_at: ISO timestamp of when enrichment completed for this row.
descriptions.first_name: Given name extracted from `editor` via the probablepeople ML name parser. Used as the lookup key for WGND 2.0 gender inference; preserved in the public release so users can re-use the parsed value without rerunning probablepeople.
descriptions.last_name: Surname extracted from `editor` via the probablepeople ML name parser. Empty when probablepeople could not parse the string; the original `editor` field is always preserved.
descriptions.gender: Country-aware inference from the editor's first name and ror_country using WGND 2.0 (Raffo & Lax-Martinez, WIPO 2021; Harvard Dataverse DOI 10.7910/DVN/MSEGSJ, roughly 3.5 million names across 195 countries). The same name can resolve differently by country (for example 'Andrea' is typically male in Italy and female in the United States). gender-guesser is a tertiary fallback for names absent from WGND. Values: male, female, unknown. The legacy 'andy' (androgynous) value was retired in v3.0.0. Self-reported gender is NOT available in this dataset; every value is inferred and should be treated as such.
descriptions.gender_prob: WGND weight in [0, 1]: the probability that an individual with this first name in this country has the inferred gender. Replaces the legacy 3-bucket {0.0, 0.75, 1.0} confidence; downstream filters should use thresholds like `>= 0.95`. For gender-guesser fallback rows, 1.0 = certain, 0.75 = mostly_*, 0.0 = unknown.
descriptions.gender_nobs: Number of observed individuals in the WGND cell (name × country) underlying the inference. Useful for filtering low-confidence cells in analysis. 0 for gender-guesser-fallback rows.
descriptions.gender_source: Provenance of the inference: `wgnd_country` (matched on first_name + ror_country, strongest signal), `wgnd_global` (matched on first_name only, used when country was missing or the country-specific cell was empty), `gender_guesser` (tertiary fallback, country-blind), or `unknown`.
descriptions.name_is_initials: True when the editor's given name is recorded only as initials (for example 'J. R. Smith'), which blocks first-name-based gender inference and weakens name-based OpenAlex matching. True on 26,763 records (2.9%). Added in v3.0.0 so these records can be excluded from name-sensitive analyses.
descriptions.orcid_n_names: Number of distinct editor name strings that map to this record's ORCID iD in the OpenAlex snapshot. 1 for a clean one-to-one iD. Supporting column for orcid_shared_flag. Added in v3.0.0.
descriptions.orcid_shared_flag: True when one ORCID iD maps to several distinct name strings in the OpenAlex snapshot, which usually signals a data-entry error at the source rather than a genuine identity. True on 246 records. Added in v3.0.0 as a transparency flag; these records are retained, not removed.
descriptions.openalex_author_id: OpenAlex Author identifier for the matched profile, restoring direct interoperability with the OpenAlex graph. Populated on 531,377 records (57.6%), which is 98.7% of the 538,490 records that matched an OpenAlex author. Added in v3.0.0; earlier releases carried the derived bibliometrics (h_index and friends) without exposing the identifier they came from.
descriptions.oa_match_method: How the OpenAlex author profile was resolved, so users can filter by match strength. Values: 'orcid' (matched on ORCID iD, the strongest signal, 344,935 records), 'name_ror' (matched on name plus the ROR-resolved institution, 107,161), 'name_only' (matched on name alone and therefore the weakest tier, most exposed to homonym error, 86,394), and 'unmatched' (no profile found, 383,470). Added in v3.0.0.
descriptions.board_size: Total number of editors on this journal's board (number of distinct editor rows sharing the same journal).
descriptions.board_eic_count: Number of distinct current chief editors on this journal's board, repeated on every row of the journal: the people (editor_key) whose role_std is editor_in_chief and whose role_is_former is False. A journal is a publisher and journal title pair here; board_size and the other board columns group by the title alone, so two journals that share a title under different publishers share those. 0 means no current chief was collected for the board (4,444 journals), 1 a single chief (7,912), 2 or more shared leadership (2,781). Empty where board_roles_suspect is True, because that board's roles cannot be trusted.
descriptions.board_roles_suspect: True on every row of a journal whose board names current chief editors (role_std editor_in_chief, role_is_former False) for at least 50% of its people, on a board of at least 10 people (distinct editor_key, former members included; a journal is a publisher and journal title pair). On such a board the collector most likely carried the first 'Editor-in-Chief' heading over the whole board, so its roles cannot be trusted: role_std is left as the role rule gives it, journal-level fallbacks included, with no further correction, and board_eic_count is empty. Leave these journals out of analyses by role. True for 56 journals (2,158 records).
descriptions.board_pct_female: Percentage (0 to 100) of female editors on this journal's board. The denominator is the RESOLVED gender count (male + female), not total board size, so the value is not artificially depressed on boards where many editors have unknown inferred gender. Fixed in v3.0.0: in v2.6.0 and v2.7.0 this column was constant at 0 because a gender-wipe regression emptied the inputs to the board-statistics stage. Any analysis using board_pct_female from those releases must be re-run.
descriptions.board_country_count: Number of distinct ror_country values on the board.
descriptions.board_country_hhi: Herfindahl–Hirschman Index of country concentration. Sum of squared country shares on the board. 0 = maximally diverse across many countries; 1 = all editors from a single country.
descriptions.board_institution_count: Number of distinct ror_id values on the board.
descriptions.board_mean_h_index: Arithmetic mean of h_index across board members with a resolved OpenAlex profile.
descriptions.editor_key: Composite identity key used to deduplicate editors across boards; the basis for the 731,251 unique-editor count. Resolved in priority order and prefixed with the tier that produced it: 'orcid:<orcid>|<ror>' when an ORCID iD is available (346,691 records, 249,699 unique editors); 'ror:<ror_id>|<name>' when there is no iD but the affiliation resolved to ROR (407,958 records, 326,043 unique); 'aff:<affiliation>|<name>' otherwise (167,311 records, 155,509 unique, of which 51,695 have an empty affiliation and so fall back to name alone). Published in v3.0.0 at reviewer request so the unique-editor count is reproducible without reconstructing the key. Because the lowest tier is name-based, distinct people who share a name and affiliation string can still collide there; the ORCID and ROR tiers are the reliable ones.
descriptions.boards_count: Number of distinct editorial boards this editor serves on in the dataset.
descriptions.publishers_count: Number of distinct publishers this editor serves across.
